candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.19 (c. 350 AD)

'I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High' (LXX 81:6 — egō eipa theoi este kai huioi hypsistou pantes) — Athanasius marks Ps 82:6 as the THEŌSIS-BY-GRACE anchor — explicitly cited by the Word himself at Jn 10:34-35 to silence the blasphemy-charge for his ego eimi self-identification. The human-recipients of the divine-word are called 'gods' by-participation, by-grace, by-econoomic-divine-naming; the Word is God by-nature, by-essence, by-eternal-generation. Athanasius's signature theōsis-formula in DI §54 — 'He was made man that we might be made God' (autos enēnthrōpēsen hina hēmeis theopoiēthōmen) — rests on this Ps 82:6 / Exo 7:1 / 2 Pet 1:4 grammar: gods-by-grace through-the-Word who-is-God-by-nature. The Tewahedo soteriology preserves this asymmetric grammar at every catechetical level.
